rationale: The open gap asks whether the off-main-thread execution of the fast path ever produces a harmful outcome. Rather than hunt for a race window that may not be winnable, this turn targets a facet of the same handler that is deterministic and that the earlier reasoning walked past: processHeartbeat checks the node's shutdown channel first and returns without responding when it is closed, while the transport that dispatched the request waits for a response on the channel it supplied. The state that exposes it is ordinary - a caller that shuts the node down without waiting on the shutdown future leaves the transport open, and the node's own shutdown future is what closes it. So the harness builds the same single node over the same fast-path transport, delivers one heartbeat while the node is live as a control, then shuts the node down without closing the transport and delivers another heartbeat with a term one above the node's current term, recording whether a response ever arrives inside a bounded interval and whether the term moved. The term operand is what makes the outcome interpretable rather than merely timed: if the handler returned at its shutdown check, no term logic ran and the term stays put, whereas a response plus a term change would mean the handler ran normally and the suspicion is defeated. I record the question as a gap on the same investigation rather than as a new one, and I do not assert anything about the outcome until the receipt exists.

gaps.question: When a heartbeat is delivered on the transport fast path while the Raft node is shut down but its transport is still open, does the caller ever receive a response, and does the handler's shutdown check prevent the term logic from running?

scope.description: On one real single-node Raft instance built over a transport that implements the heartbeat fast path, deliver one empty heartbeat while the node is live as a control, then shut the node down while leaving its transport open and deliver a second empty heartbeat, emitting one CA_EVENT JSON line that records whether each delivery got a response, how long the second waited, and the node's term and state around each.
assumptions: The wrapper transport reproduces the network transport's classification, synchronous dispatch to the installed handler and response wait faithfully, so the handler under test is the production processHeartbeat and the appendEntries it calls.

Calling Shutdown() without waiting on the returned future leaves the in-memory transport open, which is the state a caller creates when it does not wait, and the transport is only closed when the shutdown future is waited on at the end of the test.

The second heartbeat carries a term one above the node's current term, so if the handler ran its term logic the term would move and be observable; a term that stays put together with no response is evidence the handler returned at its shutdown check.

A bounded response wait is the only practical way to observe a missing response in-process; the zero-response reading is interpreted together with the source fact that the handler has no other response path once the shutdown channel is closed.

experiment.prefix: The harness (draft/assurance_generated_test.go) is one TestAssurance-prefixed test in the captured package plus a local transport wrapper. It creates a real in-memory transport, wraps it in a type that stores the handler set by NewRaft and dispatches strictly empty AppendEntries requests to it on the caller's goroutine before waiting on the supplied response channel, bootstraps a single-voter configuration with BootstrapCluster and starts the node with NewRaft over in-memory stores, snapshots and MockFSM, then waits (bounded) for Leader state. It records the term, delivers an empty heartbeat one term above it through the wrapper's fast path with a bounded wait and records the control outcome, term and state. It then calls Shutdown() and deliberately does not wait on the returned future, sleeps briefly so the node's routines observe the shutdown, records the term and state, and delivers a second empty heartbeat one term above the current one with a bounded wait, recording whether a response arrived, how long the wait was and whether the term moved. It prints one CA_EVENT JSON line with all of these operands and only then waits on the shutdown future, which is what closes the transport.
